memory_update.text: Add GXO as the reference leader for scaled reverse-logistics and ecommerce fulfillment exposure, but do not treat it as the primary underfollowed alpha lane.
Add LQDT as the cleanest small-cap underfollowed public mapping to liquidation marketplaces and reverse supply-chain services for retail returns and surplus goods.
Add TDUP as a small-cap recommerce platform candidate; survival depends on unit economics, processing automation, RaaS growth, and resale sell-through.
Add SPSC as a second-order software/network candidate for retailer integration density; returns-specific workflow evidence is required before it survives later layers.

Returns/reverse-logistics exposure splits into at least four public-market buckets: physical 3PL processing, liquidation marketplaces, managed recommerce platforms, and retail integration/data networks.
Later layers should verify profitability of returns volume, because higher returns can be margin-dilutive for logistics and recommerce operators if processing costs exceed recovery-value gains.

node: Ecommerce returns, recommerce, liquidation, and reverse-logistics infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the returns/reverse-logistics node. The cleanest reference exposure is GXO as a scaled contract-logistics operator with explicit reverse-logistics facilities and ecommerce positioning. The underfollowed discovery lane is stronger in Liquidity Services, ThredUp, and SPS Commerce: each maps to a different part of the returns/recommerce stack, respectively liquidation marketplaces, managed apparel resale, and retail trading-partner integration software. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
